cards.q: What are the PIM DR and Assert mechanisms for?
cards.a: The DR is a designated router elected on a multi-access LAN that acts for hosts (IGMP/joins and sparse-mode registering), while the Assert mechanism resolves duplicate forwarding when two routers forward the same (S,G) onto the LAN.

cards.q: How is the PIM Designated Router elected?
cards.a: The router with the highest PIM neighbor priority (default 1) wins, and on a tie the router with the highest IP address wins; priority is set with ip pim dr-priority.

cards.q: What is the role of the DR in PIM-SM?
cards.a: The DR is the single representative for the LAN: it sends IGMP/PIM joins, acts as the First-Hop Router registering the source if the source is on that LAN, and is the Last-Hop Router for the SPT join.
A PIM Assert is triggered when two routers are both forwarding the same (S,G) onto the same LAN, causing duplicated frames; the assert selects a single forwarder and the loser prunes.

cards.q: How is the PIM Assert winner decided?
cards.a: The winner is the router with the better, lower route metric to the source (lower administrative preference and lower metric); on a tie the router with the highest IP address wins.
The interface command ip pim dr-priority sets the DR priority that influences the DR election on the segment.

cards.q: Which commands verify DR and Assert state?
cards.a: show ip pim interface, show ip pim neighbor, show ip pim assert, show ip mroute, and debug ip pim.

cards.q: There is duplicate multicast traffic on a shared LAN segment; what is likely wrong?
cards.a: Two PIM routers are both forwarding the same (S,G) and the Assert mechanism has not resolved a winner, likely because their metrics to the source are equal or the assert is still pending; check show ip pim assert.

cards.q: What is the key exam distinction between DR election and PIM Assert?
cards.a: DR election determines who speaks for hosts on a LAN (priority then highest IP), while Assert determines which router forwards a duplicated (S,G) onto the LAN (lower metric then higher IP).

cards.q: What is the DR and Assert quick-review summary?
cards.a: The DR is chosen by highest priority then highest IP and handles IGMP/joins and sparse-mode registering for the LAN, while Assert keeps only the router with the lower metric to the source (higher IP on a tie) as the single forwarder to stop duplicate multicast.
